title: Trace proxy sidecar for conditional sampling and cost-aware SLO hinting
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: Trace ingestion costs are rising and burn-rate alerts are noisy due to high-cardinality traces and uniformly high sampling. We need a way to reduce trace volume while preserving signal for SLO degradation, anomaly detection, and post-incident debugging.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight trace-proxy sidecar that sits in front of existing tracing clients at the service boundary. The proxy will: (1) perform conditional sampling rules based on request attributes (route, customer tier, latency percentile), (2) attach SLO hint headers (service, route, SLO-id, weight) into trace/metric payloads for more precise burn-rate attribution, (3) emit compact telemetry and sampling stats to metrics pipelines, and (4) expose a runtime-config API (feature flags + rollout percentages) for gradual deployment and experiments.

Why this approach: Centralizing sampling logic in a proxy avoids changing every service SDK, enables cost-aware policies across the fleet, and provides the observability platform rich contextual hints to compute burn-rate and anomaly scores without ingesting full traces for every request.

Scope: Sidecar implementation (Go), integration adapters for OpenTelemetry/Jaeger/Zipkin clients, runtime configuration via Config Service, pipeline enrichment to consume SLO hints, dashboard changes to surface sampling coverage and hint-derived burn-rate adjustments, and a canary rollout plan with metrics/latency guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar runs as a local process and accepts OTLP/HTTP traces from instrumented services
Conditional sampling rules implement route/customer-tier/latency predicates and are configurable via runtime API
SLO hint headers are propagated to the metrics pipeline and used by burn-rate calculator in the observability backend
end-to-end deployment to a single non-prod cluster with sampling rules enabled and telemetry visible in sampling-coverage dashboard
Trace ingestion volume reduced by at least 15% in canary without missing any incidents from last-30d that previously triggered burn-rate alerts
No added 95th-percentile tail latency > 1.5ms at the service socket for proxied traffic
Runbook updated and oncall trained; rollback plan validated in DR drill
work_notes: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with platform, runtime, and oncall. Agreed to prototype as user-space sidecar to avoid kernel changes.
2026-03-11: PoC: simple HTTP proxy that reads trace attributes and applies a deterministic sampling hash. Observed negligible latency (median +0.2ms) in local perf tests.
2026-03-11: Decided to standardize SLO hint schema: slo_id, slo_weight, route_id, reason. Will be attached as trace attributes and emitted as metric tags.
2026-03-12: Platform team requested an internal metrics event for every sampled decision to feed sampling-coverage dashboard. Added as next step.
2026-03-12: Security reviewed sidecar networking model; no new outbound hosts required. Config service auth flow approved by Security (token-based, short-lived).
comments: Priya Kapoor (2026-03-10): PM note: Priority driven by rising trace costs and recent false positive burn-rate alerts for Search. Need measurable cost reduction and no loss in signal for high-sev incidents.
Marco Ruiz (Observability SRE) (2026-03-11): SRE feedback: Ensure sampling decisions are reproducible for replay; include original trace-id in downstream metrics to allow later correlation.
Dana Li (Runtime Eng) (2026-03-11): Runtime comment: Kernel bypass not required currently; keep initial implementation in user-space and revisit if CPU overhead becomes material.
Avery Chen (2026-03-12): Implementation note: PoC repo at github.com/redwood/trace-proxy/poc. Prototype uses deterministic FNV hash over route+user_id for sticky sampling.

Elena M. (Oncall Lead) (2026-03-12): Oncall requirements: dashboard must show per-service sampling rate and fraction of errors within sampled vs unsampled buckets. Add alert if sampling skews error coverage > 10%.
Priya Kapoor (2026-03-12): PM follow-up: Add A/B experiment plan to quantify reduction in burn-rate false positives and effect on anomaly detection precision/recall.
notes_for_review: Request code review from runtime team for sidecar resource limits; request SRE to validate burn-rate integration test harness. Prioritize a small non-prod canary before any prod rollout.
open_questions: Should sampling decisions be deterministic per customer ID or per request to maximize debugging fidelity?
Do we need to persist sampling-decisions for up to 24h to allow retroactive rehydration of traces for incidents?
What is the acceptable floor for sampling of P0 customers (should be 100% or configurable?)
